agent self-reported invariants_ok=false: Two rubric-data inconsistencies were found (not grading errors on our part, but worth flagging for the gold-set): (1) For criterion 'b', the evidence_requirements text computes the calibrated Human-Gorilla divergence as '4.0% × 2 Mya/1% = 8.0 Mya' (consistent with the stimulus table's stated 4.0% figure), but the minimum_fix/accepted_variants fields reference a different figure ('2.1% × 2 Mya/% = ~4.2 Mya'), which does not match the 4.0% given in this item's stimulus — likely a leftover from a different item version. We graded the student's calculation (4.0%×2=8.0 Mya) against the stimulus-consistent 8.0 Mya figure in evidence_requirements, which the student matched exactly. (2) For criteria 'a', 'b', and 'c', the free-text point breakdowns embedded in evidence_requirements (e.g. 'a: 1 pt for synapomorphy definition + cladogram topology; 1 pt for parsimony explanation') describe more discrete sub-points than the criterion's actual points_possible column value (a=1, b=3, c=3), so the prose and the DB point allocations don't line up 1:1. We scored holistically against points_possible as recorded in frq_criteria (the authoritative field), awarding full credit for each criterion only where the response substantively covered all the content described in evidence_requirements.
